full_judgment:
5. The Administrative Tribunal; Dhaka allowed the case of the petitioner by its judgment and order 24.10.2004. Against that judgment and order,  the respondents preferred A.A.T Appeal No.22 of 2005 in the Administrative Appellate Tribunal, Dhaka which allowed the appeal by its judgment and order dated 05.02.2009 setting aside the judgment and order dated 24.10.2004 passed by the Administrative Tribunal, Dhaka in A.T. Case No. 244 of 2000 only on the point of limitation. 

 8. The learned Advocate-on-Record for, the petitioner submits that careful perusal of the case record being placed in juxtaposition with the third proviso to section 4(2) of the Administrative Tribunal Act, 1980 (Act. VII of 1981) transpired that the higher departmental authority (Board of Directors) passed order on 05.06.2000 rejecting the prayer for re-instating the petitioner in service and as per third proviso to section 4(2) of the Act, the limitation. started running from that day and the petitioner is entitled to the benefit of that proviso and hence the Appellate Tribunal erred in law in holding that second proviso to section 4(2) of the Act applies, which has got no manner of application in this case and as such the impugned judgment and order is liable to be set aside. 

 10. Therefore, leave is granted to consider the following point: 1. Whether a careful perusal of the case record being placed in juxtaposition with the third proviso to section 4(2) of the Administrative Tribunals Act, 1980 (Act V.11. of 1981) trail spared that the higher departmental authority (Board of Directors) passed order on 05.06.2000 rejecting the prayer for re-instatement of the petitioner in service and as per third proviso to section 4(2) the Act, the limitation started running from that day and the petitioner is entitled to the benefit of that proviso and hence the Appellate Tribunal erred in law in holding that the second proviso to section 4(2) of the Act applies, which has got no manner of application in this .case and as such the impugned judgment and order is liable to be set aside.
